title: Romans admit forensic sense: Rom 2:13 factores legis
source_text: XIX. Imo in ipsis Pauli Epistolis occurrunt quaedam loca, ubi Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae fatentur & observant justificandi vocem accipi forensi significatione. Talis est locus qui habetur Rom. 2. 13. Factores legis justificabuntur. Ad quem Estius in suis Commentariis notat justificari idem illic esse quod justum haberi, sive declarari, usitatissima phrasi Scripturae, ut ipse loquitur. Adeoque juxta ipsum, sensus illius loci est, Qui legem satis observant justi judicabuntur, declarabuntur, habebuntur a Deo. Quam interpretationem probat quoque Ruardus Tapperus ad Art. 8. pag. 32. Circa praedicta, inquit, considerandum est, quod in Scripturis justificari non solum significat, justitia imbui, donari & ornari, sed quandoque etiam justum pronunciari, declarari, judicari, comprobari ac deputari. Secundum quam significationem interpretatur beatus Augustinus sententiam Apostoli Pauli, Factores legis justificabuntur, id est, inquit, justi habebuntur, justi deputabuntur.
pass_a_gloss: Nay, in Paul's Epistles themselves certain places occur where the Doctors of the Roman Church confess and observe that the word of justifying is taken in a forensic signification. Such is the place in Rom. 2:13. The doers of the law shall be justified. On which Estius in his Commentaries notes that to be justified there is the same as to be held or declared just, by a most usual phrase of Scripture, as he himself speaks. And so according to him the sense of that place is: Those who sufficiently observe the law shall be judged, declared, held just by God. Which interpretation Ruardus Tapperus also approves at Art. 8 p. 32. Concerning the aforesaid, he says, it is to be considered that in the Scriptures to be justified does not only signify to be imbued, gifted, and adorned with righteousness, but sometimes also to be pronounced, declared, judged, approved, and reckoned just. According to which signification blessed Augustine interprets the sentence of the Apostle Paul, The doers of the law shall be justified—that is, he says, they shall be held just, reckoned just.
pass_b_english: Romans themselves grant forensic justify at Rom 2:13 (Estius: held/declared just).
Tapper + Augustine: sometimes pronounce/reckon just, not only gift with righteousness.
